summary:
## Idea
An explicit traversal stack computes strongly connected components without recursive call depth. cycles keeps multi-node components and singleton self-loops.

## Complexity
O(V+E) expected work and O(V+E) stored graph/traversal data, assuming expected constant-time structural hashing and bounded callback work.

## Use when
Find dependency cycles or collapse a directed graph into components.

## Avoid when
Undirected connectivity alone suffices; UnionFind is the simpler interface there.

## Pitfalls
Duplicate nodes keep their first occurrence; successors outside the declared node set are ignored. Deterministic input orders determine component order. A long acyclic path must not consume the runtime call stack.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Algorithms; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Algorithms.Graph.Scc.cycles: 'N list -> ('N -> 'N list) -> 'N list list when 'N: equality`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Graph
let next n = if n = 1 then [2] else [1]
let cycles = Scc.cycles [1; 2] next
```

## Tests
SccTests: recursive Tarjan and reachability-closure oracles, duplicate/outside-node cases, 100000-node chain and ring.

## Bench
The cited archived 0.2.0 baseline contains graph/iterative-tarjan-scc/random-digraph. Read its source commit, host/date/toolchain, sizes, work counts, runtime-specific median/p95 and spread. These are GitHub-hosted runner-class comparisons, not quiet-host absolute performance; this later source revision is not itself remeasured.
